stem: A multinational engineering organisation has dozens of reusable agent skills with approved instructions, scripts and documentation. Many teams need to discover and reuse them, and the platform team must control which version agents load by default and roll back quickly if a release misbehaves. What should they use?

options.A: Skill Registry: immutable skill revisions plus a default revision pointer
options.B: A shared Cloud Storage bucket of skill folders with object versioning enabled
options.C: Agent Designer templates that embed each skill's instructions
options.D: A Git repository per team, with each team copying skills they like into their own repo

rationale.A: Skill Registry stores skills with immutable revisions and a default revision pointer that can be changed to deploy or roll back a version.
rationale.B: Storage versioning is not discovery, and agents have no notion of a default revision.
rationale.C: Low-code agent templates are not a skill distribution mechanism for coding agents.
rationale.D: Creates the independent copies the platform team wants to avoid.

stem: A team runs a non-ADK custom agent on Agent Runtime and wants the same traces and dashboards as their ADK agents. What must they do?

options.A: Rewrite the agent with ADK, the only framework that can be traced
options.B: Export logs to BigQuery and rebuild the dashboards there
options.C: Nothing: Agent Runtime instruments any deployed agent automatically
options.D: Instrument the app to emit OpenTelemetry telemetry

rationale.A: Non-ADK agents can be instrumented too.
rationale.B: Duplicates tooling instead of using the platform's observability.
rationale.C: Built-in components emit telemetry, but custom applications must be instrumented.
rationale.D: Agents must be configured to send telemetry in the OpenTelemetry format to populate observability dashboards, topologies and traces; docs cover instrumenting non-ADK agents.

stem: A defence contractor is building an agent that summarises classified-adjacent engineering reports. Policy requires that prompts and outputs never leave the company's Google Cloud project and VPC, and the security team must control the serving environment. Quality needs are moderate. Which model strategy fits?

options.A: Call a proprietary model through its serverless model-as-a-service endpoint, relying on standard terms
options.B: Run inference on developer laptops with a quantised model and sync results to the project
options.C: Fine-tune the largest available proprietary model so it no longer needs external calls
options.D: Self-deploy an open model from Model Garden into the project, served inside the VPC

rationale.A: Serverless MaaS does not give the team control of the serving environment the policy requires.
rationale.B: Moves sensitive data onto endpoints outside the controlled environment.
rationale.C: Tuning does not move serving into the project, and the largest model is not needed for moderate quality.
rationale.D: Self-deployed Model Garden models run in your project and VPC network with full control of the serving environment, unlike serverless model-as-a-service offerings.

stem: A regulator asks a bank to demonstrate, for a sample of automated decisions, who approved them and what the approver saw. The agent currently records only that a human clicked approve. What should be added?

options.A: Require two approvers so the decision is harder to dispute
options.B: Increase log retention for the existing approval events to seven years
options.C: Store the model's reasoning text as the record of the decision
options.D: Record the action, the context shown and the approver identity with each decision

rationale.A: More approvers without context does not answer the regulator's question.
rationale.B: Keeping insufficient records longer does not make them sufficient.
rationale.C: Model reasoning is not evidence of human review.
rationale.D: An auditable human-in-the-loop trail must capture what was presented, who decided and what was decided, not merely that approval occurred.

stem: Employees upload PDFs and spreadsheets into Gemini Enterprise chats with an agent. Security wants uploaded documents screened for prompt injection and sensitive data before the model uses them. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Enable Model Armor on Agent Gateway, which screens attachments for all runtimes
options.B: Use Model Armor's Gemini Enterprise integration, which supports document screening
options.C: Model Armor cannot read documents, so convert every page to an image first
options.D: Run Sensitive Data Protection jobs on the upload bucket after each chat ends

rationale.A: The docs state document screening is only integrated with Gemini Enterprise.
rationale.B: Model Armor document screening (PDF, CSV, DOCX, XLSX and others) is integrated only with Gemini Enterprise.
rationale.C: Documents are supported content; converting them adds work and image limits apply.
rationale.D: Scanning after the model has used the content does not prevent the risk.

stem: A support agent's transcripts are stored for quality review, and the privacy team wants identifiers removed from stored transcripts while keeping them readable for analysis. Which service handles this?

options.A: Cloud Logging exclusion filters on the transcript sink
options.B: Agent Gateway egress policy on the storage API
options.C: Sensitive Data Protection de-identification
options.D: Model Armor floor settings applied to the storage bucket

rationale.A: Excluding logs discards data instead of de-identifying transcripts.
rationale.B: Authorization does not transform stored content.
rationale.C: Sensitive Data Protection inspects data for sensitive elements and can de-identify it while preserving analytical utility.
rationale.D: Model Armor screens prompts and responses in the request path, not stored objects.

stem: An insurance company built a claims-triage agent in Agent Designer. Given a claim description, it must decide whether the claim is covered by checking four policy conditions. The agent often states a verdict that contradicts one of the conditions it quoted. Business users can only change the agent's instructions in the console. What should you do?

options.A: Split the agent into four agents, one per condition, and ask the claims handler to consult each of them
options.B: Attach the full policy document as a data source so the agent can retrieve the exact condition wording
options.C: Instruct it to check each condition in turn before the verdict, with two worked examples
options.D: Instruct the agent to answer with only 'covered' or 'not covered' so it has fewer chances to contradict itself

rationale.A: Pushes orchestration onto users and does not address the reasoning pattern.
rationale.B: The agent already quotes the conditions correctly; the failure is in reasoning over them, not retrieval.
rationale.C: Chain-of-thought style instructions plus few-shot examples are the in-console prompt techniques the guide names for improving multi-condition reasoning.
rationale.D: Suppressing reasoning usually makes multi-step decisions worse, not better.

stem: A security team must guarantee a minimum screening level for every Model Armor template any project team creates, while letting teams add stricter settings for their own applications. What should they configure?

options.A: A single shared template that every application must reference
options.B: Inspect-only mode everywhere, with teams enabling blocking voluntarily
options.C: An organisation policy constraint listing required filters
options.D: Floor settings at the project level, with per-application templates on top

rationale.A: One template cannot express per-application strictness and can be bypassed by new templates.
rationale.B: Voluntary enforcement is not a guarantee.
rationale.C: Not the mechanism Model Armor provides for minimum enforcement.
rationale.D: Floor settings establish minimum requirements for all templates created at the project level, while templates configure per-application filters.

stem: A team runs `adk eval` entirely offline in a hermetic CI container with no Google Cloud project configured. Most criteria work, but one fails with an authentication error. Which criterion most likely requires the cloud?

options.A: response_match_score, which fetches the ROUGE implementation at run time
options.B: safety_v1, which delegates to the Agent Platform Eval SDK
options.C: adk conformance, which uploads baselines to the platform
options.D: tool_trajectory_avg_score, which calls the platform to compare trajectories

rationale.A: ROUGE-1 overlap is computed locally.
rationale.B: safety_v1 delegates to the Agent Platform Eval SDK and requires Google Cloud setup, unlike purely local criteria.
rationale.C: Conformance compares against a local golden baseline.
rationale.D: Trajectory matching is computed locally without an LLM judge.

stem: A 'release-notes' subagent should be able to run `git log` but nothing else in the terminal, while the parent agent keeps its broader command permissions. Which subagent configuration addresses this?

options.A: Rely on inheritance: subagents always get stricter command permissions than parents
options.B: Set commandExecutionPolicy in the subagent's front matter to allow only git log
options.C: Put 'only run git log' in the subagent's description field
options.D: Disable the terminal sandbox for the subagent so policies apply correctly

rationale.A: Subagents inherit the parent's allowed command prefixes; tightening needs explicit configuration.
rationale.B: Subagent front matter supports tools, model and commandExecutionPolicy to shape what the subagent may execute.
rationale.C: The description is for selection and documentation, not enforcement.
rationale.D: Removing the sandbox reduces isolation and does not restrict commands.

stem: After rolling out Claude Code on Google Cloud to 200 engineers, the team sees frequent HTTP 429 errors during the morning stand-up rush. Authentication and model access are confirmed working. What is the most likely remediation?

options.A: Rotate the developers' gcloud credentials, because expired tokens surface as rate-limit errors
options.B: Move the developers' workstations into a VPC Service Controls perimeter to prioritise traffic
options.C: Request a quota increase for the Claude models in the region the developers use
options.D: Switch every developer to a personal Anthropic API key to spread requests across accounts

rationale.A: Expired credentials produce authentication errors, not 429 rate limiting.
rationale.B: A perimeter controls data exfiltration; it does not raise model quotas.
rationale.C: Claude Code generates 429 errors when the project's model quotas are too low for the traffic.
rationale.D: Abandons the centralised billing and governance the rollout was for.

stem: A developer's new Antigravity CLI plugin directory contains skills/, hooks.json and mcp_config.json, but `agy plugin install` rejects it. Which file is most likely missing?

options.A: settings.json inside the plugin directory
options.B: plugin.json, the required manifest
options.C: AGENTS.md at the root of the plugin directory
options.D: SKILL.md at the root of the plugin directory

rationale.A: settings.json is the user's primary configuration, not a plugin requirement.
rationale.B: plugin.json is the required manifest; its name must match the allowed pattern.
rationale.C: Rules live under rules/; AGENTS.md is not the plugin manifest.
rationale.D: SKILL.md belongs inside each skill, not at the plugin root.

stem: A team wants some fields in their Agent Retrieval collection to be validated strictly while allowing additional ad-hoc fields on some documents during a migration. What does the service offer?

options.A: Schema definitions supporting both strict and relaxed validation
options.B: Strict validation only, so all documents must match one schema
options.C: Schema enforcement only on vector fields, never on payload fields
options.D: No schema support; every document is an opaque blob

rationale.A: Data objects in collections have schema definitions supporting strict and relaxed validation.
rationale.B: Relaxed validation is supported.
rationale.C: Validation covers the data object's fields generally.
rationale.D: Collections define schemas over JSON data objects.

stem: A public-sector agency's Agent Designer agent summarises citizen complaints for caseworkers. The summaries must use a fixed structure (issue, location, urgency, requested action), never include the citizen's phone number, and flag uncertainty instead of guessing urgency. Which instruction design is best?

options.A: Twenty example summaries in the prompt and no written rules, so the model infers the conventions
options.B: A single instruction to 'summarise each complaint professionally', relying on the model's defaults
options.C: State the format, the no-contact-details rule and an 'unclear' fallback, plus one example
options.D: An instruction to think step by step and show the caseworker its full reasoning for each summary

rationale.A: Examples alone may not generalise the privacy and uncertainty rules to unseen inputs.
rationale.B: Leaves format, privacy and uncertainty handling to chance.
rationale.C: Clear role, format, constraints and an explicit fallback, reinforced by an example, is the standard way to guide behaviour with system instructions and templates.
rationale.D: Chain-of-thought can help reasoning but exposing it adds noise and does not enforce format or privacy.

stem: A team lets its coding agent drive Agents CLI while developing, but release engineers want the production deployment in the pipeline to run the same commands deterministically, with no model deciding what to do. How does Agents CLI support this?

options.A: Human mode: the same agents-cli commands run directly in scripts or a terminal
options.B: Recording the agent's session once and replaying the transcript in CI
options.C: A separate deployment-only CLI, because Agents CLI requires a coding agent to run
options.D: Agent mode with temperature zero, so the coding agent makes the same choices each time

rationale.A: Agents CLI supports agent mode (coding assistants run the commands using skills) and human mode (deterministic control running commands in terminals or scripts).
rationale.B: Replaying a transcript is not a supported, deterministic deployment mechanism.
rationale.C: The same CLI runs without a coding agent in human mode.
rationale.D: Still model-driven; the requirement is no model in the loop.

stem: An analytics agent runs model-generated Python over customer data. Which combination of controls best limits the damage if the generated code is malicious or buggy? (Choose two.)

options.A: Log the generated code and review it weekly
options.B: Execute the code in an isolated sandbox with no standing credentials
options.C: Ask the model to review its own code for safety before running it
options.D: Restrict egress from the execution environment to approved destinations
options.E: Run the code with the agent's own service account for simplicity

rationale.A: After-the-fact review does not prevent the damage.
rationale.B: Isolation and credential-free execution prevent generated code from reaching other systems.
rationale.C: Self-review by the same system that wrote the code is not a control.
rationale.D: Network restrictions stop exfiltration even if the code runs successfully.
rationale.E: Gives generated code the agent's full permissions.

stem: A team new to RAG must explain the pipeline to stakeholders in the order the stages run for RAG Engine. Which sequence is correct?

options.A: Ingestion, indexing, embedding, chunking, generation, retrieval
options.B: Ingestion, chunking, embedding, indexing, retrieval, generation
options.C: Chunking, generation, embedding, retrieval, indexing, ingestion
options.D: Embedding, ingestion, retrieval, chunking, indexing, generation

rationale.A: Chunking precedes embedding, and retrieval precedes generation.
rationale.B: RAG Engine documents data ingestion, transformation, embedding, indexing into a corpus, retrieval and generation in that order.
rationale.C: Generation is the final stage, not the second.
rationale.D: Embedding cannot precede ingesting and chunking the data.

stem: A reviewer asks how Agent Gateway and the auth manager keep end-user credentials away from agent code while still letting the agent call an external API on the user's behalf. What is the mechanism?

options.A: The agent receives a short-lived copy of the token and discards it after the call
options.B: Credentials are encrypted by the auth manager and decrypted at the gateway on egress
options.C: The gateway issues the agent a service-account key scoped to the external API
options.D: The user pastes the token into the conversation, which is redacted from logs

rationale.A: The agent still handles the raw credential, which is what the design avoids.
rationale.B: End-user credentials are encrypted by the auth manager and decrypted at the gateway, so the agent never accesses the raw credential.
rationale.C: Keys are not how user-delegated access is handled here.
rationale.D: Puts a live credential into conversation data.

stem: An agent on Cloud Run has outgrown its hand-rolled session and memory code, which now causes most incidents. The team wants to keep its container build but stop maintaining state code. What is the pragmatic path?

options.A: Rewrite the agent in ADK and deploy to Agent Runtime immediately
options.B: Move state into the container's local disk to simplify the architecture
options.C: Add a Memorystore cache in front of the existing session code
options.D: Keep the container and adopt managed Sessions and Memory Bank for state

rationale.A: A full rewrite is a large step when only state management is the problem.
rationale.B: Local disk is lost on restart and breaks with multiple instances.
rationale.C: A cache does not remove the custom state code or its bugs.
rationale.D: Managed session and memory services can be used from an agent running elsewhere, removing the custom code without a rewrite.

stem: An internal agent generates Python to analyse uploaded CSV files and runs it on GKE. A red-team test shows generated code could reach the Kubernetes API server and a metadata endpoint. What should you adopt for the execution step?

options.A: A larger node pool so generated code has dedicated CPU and memory
options.B: Running the generated code in the agent's own container to reduce hops
options.C: GKE Agent Sandbox, for process, storage and network isolation of generated code
options.D: A system prompt instructing the model not to generate network calls

rationale.A: Resources are not isolation.
rationale.B: Puts untrusted code next to the agent's credentials, making it worse.
rationale.C: Agent Sandbox mitigates the risk of untrusted code interfering with other apps or the node by providing strong process, storage and network isolation.
rationale.D: Prompts do not constrain what generated code can do at runtime.

stem: A data team wants an internal agent to answer questions over a curated BigQuery table of product specifications, and only engineers in specific groups may see rows about unreleased products. The team wants access checks performed by the search layer rather than by agent code. Which statement is true?

options.A: Access control exists only for Google Drive, so the table must be exported to Drive first
options.B: The agent must filter rows by group membership in an after-tool callback
options.C: BigQuery row-level security is carried automatically into Agent Search results
options.D: Agent Search supports access-controlled data stores for BigQuery sources

rationale.A: BigQuery is explicitly supported.
rationale.B: Possible, but it is exactly the application-side enforcement the team wants to avoid.
rationale.C: Search results are governed by the data store's ACLs; do not assume source-side policies propagate.
rationale.D: Access control is available for Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Google Drive and all third-party data sources.

stem: After a regional incident, an agent returned errors for 40 minutes. The postmortem asks how to reduce impact next time without doubling steady-state cost. Which measure fits best?

options.A: Degrade gracefully with caching and reduced capability
options.B: Retry failed requests indefinitely until the region recovers
options.C: Send users to a status page and disable the agent during incidents
options.D: Run a hot standby of the full stack in a second region at all times

rationale.A: A defined degraded mode keeps partial service without running full duplicate capacity at all times.
rationale.B: Amplifies load and leaves users waiting.
rationale.C: No service at all, when partial service was achievable.
rationale.D: Meets availability but doubles steady-state cost, which was excluded.

stem: A finance team wants a Gemini Enterprise agent that runs every Monday at 07:00, pulls the previous week's expense reports from a connected source, flags anomalies, and waits for a manager to approve flagged items before emailing a summary. Nobody on the team writes code. What should they build?

options.A: A scheduled Agent Designer workflow with a human-intervention step before the email
options.B: An ADK agent deployed to Agent Runtime, triggered weekly by Cloud Scheduler with an approval tool
options.C: An Agent Designer chat agent that the manager opens every Monday morning and asks to run the review
options.D: A CX Agent Studio flow with one page per step and a no-input event handler that waits for approval

rationale.A: Agent Designer workflows combine AI steps with human intervention, support deterministic sequencing, and can be scheduled to run on a recurring basis.
rationale.B: Works technically but requires code, which the team cannot maintain.
rationale.C: Chat agents are for open-ended conversational tasks; the requirement is a scheduled, sequenced process with an approval step.
rationale.D: CX Agent Studio targets customer conversations; the internal scheduled workflow belongs in Gemini Enterprise.

stem: A marketplace's multi-agent system receives 40 million messages a day. Every message first passes a router that picks one of six specialist agents; the planner agent that follows needs strong reasoning. Latency and cost are dominated by the router today. What model design is best?

options.A: A rules-only router with no model and no planner, because models are too slow at this volume
options.B: A small, fast model for the router and a larger LLM only for the planner
options.C: A small model for the planner and the large LLM for the router, since routing is the entry point
options.D: The most capable LLM for both router and planner, so routing mistakes never happen

rationale.A: Drops the reasoning capability the planner provides.
rationale.B: Matching model size to task keeps the high-volume classification step cheap and fast while keeping reasoning quality where it matters.
rationale.C: Inverts the needs: planning requires reasoning, routing does not.
rationale.D: Pays top-tier cost and latency on 40 million simple classifications.

stem: A team generates multi-turn evaluation conversations with a simulated user. Before trusting the results, they want to check that the simulated user followed the intended conversation plan rather than drifting into unrelated requests. Which criterion applies?

options.A: multi_turn_task_success_v1 on the conversation outcome
options.B: hallucinations_v1 applied to the simulated user's messages
options.C: multi_turn_trajectory_quality_v1 on the agent's tool calls
options.D: per_turn_user_simulator_quality_v1

rationale.A: Outcome success does not confirm the simulator behaved as planned.
rationale.B: Grounding of agent responses is a different property.
rationale.C: That assesses the agent's interaction quality, not the simulator.
rationale.D: per_turn_user_simulator_quality_v1 validates that the user simulator stayed faithful to the conversation plan.

stem: An architect must pick the primary metric for a customer-facing FAQ agent whose main risk is confidently inventing policy details. Which choice best matches the risk?

options.A: Average response latency across the evalset
options.B: A grounding metric that flags unsupported statements
options.C: Token cost per answer as a proxy for verbosity
options.D: Tool trajectory exact match against a reference

rationale.A: Speed does not address invented content.
rationale.B: The named risk is fabrication, which grounding metrics measure directly.
rationale.C: Cost tells nothing about factual support.
rationale.D: An FAQ agent's risk is content, not tool ordering.

stem: Traces for a support agent show the same `lookup_order` call with identical arguments seven times in one session before the agent gives up. What is the failure, and which fix addresses it most directly?

options.A: Session state corruption: clear the session store and retry
options.B: Model drift: retrain or switch to a newer model version
options.C: A reasoning loop: cap iterations and handle the empty result explicitly
options.D: Tool latency: increase the tool's timeout so the agent waits longer

rationale.A: Nothing indicates corrupted state, and clearing it loses history.
rationale.B: Drift is a gradual quality change, not repeated identical calls in one session.
rationale.C: Repeated identical tool calls indicate a loop; bounding iterations and giving the model a defined path for empty results breaks it.
rationale.D: The calls complete; the agent simply repeats them.

stem: A payments agent intermittently returns a generic apology. Traces show a tool span with status error and no retry, and the model was given the raw stack trace as the tool result. What should change?

options.A: Instruct the model to apologise more specifically when a tool fails
options.B: Suppress tool errors so the model never sees them
options.C: Increase the model's temperature so it explores alternative phrasings
options.D: Return a structured error the model can act on, and retry transient failures

rationale.A: Improves wording without improving behaviour.
rationale.B: Hiding failures produces confident wrong answers.
rationale.C: Sampling settings do not handle tool failures.
rationale.D: Tools should surface actionable, structured errors with retries for transient faults so the agent can recover or explain precisely.

stem: Fifty engineers each run a local copy of an internal documentation MCP server in their coding agents. Versions drift, fixes take weeks to reach everyone, and security cannot see who queried what. What is the better architecture?

options.A: One remote MCP server with authentication and logging
options.B: Replace the MCP server with a rules file containing the documentation
options.C: Distribute the local server as a plugin and ask engineers to update weekly
options.D: Let each engineer's agent crawl the documentation site directly

rationale.A: A shared remote server gives one version, central access control and auditability.
rationale.B: Loses search and freshness and bloats context.
rationale.C: Still local copies with drift and no central audit.
rationale.D: No access control, no audit, and inconsistent results.

stem: An agent must query an operational AlloyDB database and a Firestore collection as part of answering customer questions. The team wants Google-managed tool endpoints rather than maintaining servers. What is available?

options.A: Only BigQuery has a managed MCP server; other databases need custom servers
options.B: Managed MCP servers exist but cannot be used by ADK agents, only by coding agents
options.C: Database access from agents must always go through a custom integration layer
options.D: Managed MCP servers for Google Cloud databases including AlloyDB and Firestore

rationale.A: Managed servers exist for several database services.
rationale.B: They are MCP endpoints usable by agents generally.
rationale.C: Managed MCP servers are the prebuilt option.
rationale.D: Google Cloud offers managed MCP servers for AlloyDB, Spanner, Cloud SQL, Firestore and Bigtable.

stem: A team is about to enable semantic governance policies in production for the first time and worries about blocking legitimate traffic. What is the recommended rollout?

options.A: Start in dry-run mode to validate the configuration without blocking
options.B: Enable enforcement for 10% of agents chosen at random
options.C: Write the policies but leave them unattached until an incident occurs
options.D: Enable enforcement and roll back if error rates rise

rationale.A: The documentation recommends deploying semantic governance policies in dry-run mode first to validate configuration without blocking traffic.
rationale.B: Partial enforcement still blocks real traffic and gives a partial view.
rationale.C: Provides no validation and no protection.
rationale.D: Causes the outage the team is trying to avoid.

stem: A furniture retailer's support agent should find the right assembly guide when a customer uploads a photo of a half-built product, and should also find short how-to video clips and text articles for the same product. The team wants one retrieval index rather than separate pipelines per media type. What should they use?

options.A: Captions generated for every image and video, embedded as text
options.B: A natively multimodal embedding model and a single vector index
options.C: Keyword search over SKUs parsed from media filenames
options.D: Separate image, video and text indexes merged by a reranker

rationale.A: Workable but lossy, and it keeps a per-media captioning pipeline the team wanted to avoid.
rationale.B: Gemini Embedding 2 maps text, images, video, audio and documents into one embedding space, enabling cross-modal retrieval from a single index.
rationale.C: A photo of a half-built product carries no SKU; this is not semantic retrieval.
rationale.D: Contradicts the one-index requirement and adds orchestration.

stem: An ADK agent's instruction contains `Answer in {language}.` Some sessions never set `language` and the agent throws an error before responding. The team wants a default behaviour instead of a crash. What should change?

options.A: Rename the placeholder to {temp:language} so it is always initialised
options.B: Remove templating and ask the model to guess the user's language
options.C: Wrap the whole instruction in a try/except inside a before_agent_callback
options.D: Use {language?} so a missing key does not raise an error

rationale.A: The temp: prefix changes scope, not whether a missing key errors.
rationale.B: Loses the explicit preference when it is set.
rationale.C: Heavy workaround for a built-in templating option.
rationale.D: Instruction templating throws when a key is missing; appending ? makes the key optional.

stem: A consulting firm wants Gemini Enterprise to answer questions using Google Drive, Gmail and Salesforce. An architect proposes exporting everything nightly into one BigQuery table and connecting that table. Why is using the native connectors the better design?

options.A: Native connectors skip permission checks, which gives more complete answers
options.B: BigQuery tables cannot be used as a Gemini Enterprise data source at all
options.C: Connectors keep each item's content, metadata and ACLs in the data store
options.D: Connectors train the model on the sources, so answers need no retrieval

rationale.A: The opposite: preserving ACLs is a key reason to use them.
rationale.B: BigQuery is a supported source; the issue is losing ACLs and freshness, not support.
rationale.C: Connectors convert source information into a standardised document format that carries content, metadata and ACLs into data stores.
rationale.D: Connectors populate data stores for retrieval; they do not train models.

stem: A team deploys three A2A agents to Agent Runtime and expects to spend a sprint wiring them into the organisation's catalog and gateway policy. What actually happens, and what is left to do?

options.A: Nothing is automatic: registration, gateway routing and policy all require manual setup
options.B: They register automatically and route through the gateway; policy still needs authoring
options.C: Everything is automatic, including a default deny-all authorization policy
options.D: Registration is automatic only after the first successful A2A call from another agent

rationale.A: Registration and gateway routing are automatic for Agent Runtime.
rationale.B: Agents on Agent Runtime register in Agent Registry automatically and their traffic goes through Agent Gateway, but authorization policies must still be configured.
rationale.C: Policies are authored by the team; they are not created for you.
rationale.D: Registration happens on deployment, not on first call.

stem: A retrieval system for a multilingual support centre returns good results in English but poor results for Portuguese and Japanese questions over the same translated documents. Chunking and reranking are already in place. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Top-k is set too low for non-English questions specifically
options.B: The vector index uses cosine similarity instead of dot product
options.C: The corpus needs to be re-indexed once per language into separate backends
options.D: The embedding model does not handle those languages well

rationale.A: A global k does not discriminate by language.
rationale.B: The distance metric does not explain a per-language gap.
rationale.C: Separate indexes are not required when the embedding model is multilingual.
rationale.D: Retrieval quality across languages depends on the embedding model's multilingual coverage.

stem: A platform team wants developers' coding agents to follow the company's agent-building conventions (project layout, evaluation thresholds, deployment approvals) whenever they use Agents CLI. The guide mentions configuring skills with Agents CLI, including plugins. What should they do?

options.A: Fork Agents CLI and hard-code the conventions into its commands
options.B: Add the conventions to the Agents CLI help text through an environment variable
options.C: Publish the conventions as a Gemini Enterprise chat agent developers can ask
options.D: Package the conventions as skills, distributed as a plugin with the Agents CLI skills

rationale.A: Maintaining a fork is costly and breaks upgrades.
rationale.B: Not a supported customisation mechanism.
rationale.C: Developers' coding agents would not use it automatically.
rationale.D: Skills and plugins are how coding agents receive packaged, reusable know-how alongside Agents CLI.

stem: A developer notices the coding agent ran `cat .env` while debugging and printed database credentials into the session. The team wants to prevent this class of command technically, not just ask the agent to avoid it. What is the best control in the Antigravity CLI?

options.A: A rule in AGENTS.md stating that .env files must never be read or printed by the agent
options.B: A skill that explains how to debug database connections without reading credentials
options.C: A deny list entry for commands that read secret files, alongside the terminal sandbox
options.D: Renaming .env to a less obvious file name so the agent is unlikely to find it

rationale.A: Rules are guidance; the agent already ignored good practice once.
rationale.B: Useful know-how, but not enforcement.
rationale.C: Allow/deny command lists and the terminal sandbox are technical controls, unlike instructions.
rationale.D: Obscurity, and the agent can still list and read the file.

stem: A high-traffic agent on Cloud Run needs (1) a sub-millisecond cache of tool responses such as exchange rates valid for 60 seconds and (2) durable conversation history that survives instance restarts and can be listed per user. The team prefers managed services. Which pairing is best?

options.A: Memorystore for Redis for both the cache and the durable conversation history
options.B: Memorystore for Redis for the short-lived cache; managed sessions for history
options.C: Cloud Storage objects for the cache, and in-memory session service for history
options.D: BigQuery for the 60-second cache, and container local disk for conversation history

rationale.A: An in-memory cache is the wrong system of record for durable conversation history.
rationale.B: An in-memory store suits short-TTL caching; durable per-user history belongs in a managed session store.
rationale.C: Object storage is not a sub-millisecond cache and in-memory sessions vanish on restart.
rationale.D: Analytical warehouse latency for a hot cache, and local disk is lost with the instance.

stem: A five-person startup is launching its first production agent. It needs managed conversation state, long-term memory and built-in tracing, has no platform engineers, and wants to spend its time on agent logic. Which runtime should it choose?

options.A: Cloud Run, adding Firestore for sessions and a custom memory service
options.B: Compute Engine instances behind a load balancer, scaled manually
options.C: GKE with a dedicated node pool and a service mesh for the agent
options.D: Agent Runtime, with managed sessions, memory and observability

rationale.A: Workable, but the team must build and operate state and memory themselves.
rationale.B: The heaviest operational burden of all the options.
rationale.C: Maximum control and maximum operations for a team with no platform engineers.
rationale.D: Agent Runtime is the fully managed option and includes Sessions, Memory Bank, code execution and observability without infrastructure work.

stem: A platform team registered 300 skills in Skill Registry. Agents in production should pick relevant skills based on the user's request rather than loading all 300 into context, and teams should be able to create and search skills through an agent. What provides this?

options.A: Intent-based discovery from Skill Registry, plus the built-in gcp-skill-registry skill
options.B: Agent Gateway semantic governance, which injects matching skills into prompts
options.C: A nightly job that copies the ten most-used skills into each agent image
options.D: Loading all 300 SKILL.md files into the system prompt at session start

rationale.A: Skill Registry lets agents dynamically discover and load relevant skills by intent, and ships a managed gcp-skill-registry skill to create, search and manage skills.
rationale.B: Semantic governance evaluates tool calls against policy; it does not distribute skills.
rationale.C: Static, stale, and ignores the user's intent.
rationale.D: Wastes context and cost; the registry exists to avoid this.

stem: A startup must choose a model for a legal-drafting agent. It expects to fine-tune on its own corpus, wants the option to move serving between clouds later, and has an ML team comfortable operating models. Top-tier reasoning is less important than control. Which consideration most favours an open-weights model?

options.A: Weights can be tuned, inspected and served anywhere, avoiding lock-in to one provider's API
options.B: Open-weights models never incur infrastructure costs because the weights are free
options.C: Open models always outperform proprietary models on legal reasoning benchmarks
options.D: Proprietary models cannot be used for drafting documents under any licence

rationale.A: Open weights give control over tuning, portability and serving, which are the startup's stated priorities.
rationale.B: Serving open models costs compute; the weights being free is not the same as free inference.
rationale.C: Not true in general, and reasoning quality was not the priority.
rationale.D: Incorrect; the decision is about control and portability, not a blanket prohibition.

stem: A travel company's booking flow needs the same three escape paths — 'speak to a person', 'start over', and 'cancel booking' — available on eleven different pages. Designers keep forgetting to add one of them when they create new pages. What is the most maintainable configuration?

options.A: Define the three routes once in a route group and attach it where needed
options.B: Create a webhook that inspects every utterance for the three phrases and returns the target page
options.C: Copy the three routes onto every page and add a mandatory checklist item to the design review template
options.D: Put the three phrases in the agent's system instructions so the model can handle them from any page

rationale.A: Route groups package reusable transition routes so they are defined once and attached to pages or the flow.
rationale.B: Reimplements routing in code, adds latency and failure modes, and duplicates built-in behaviour.
rationale.C: Duplication is what causes the drift described; it does not scale.
rationale.D: In a state-based flow, transitions are controlled by routes; instructions do not move the conversation between pages.

stem: A team enables Model Armor on a new agent but wants two weeks of evidence about false positives before anything is blocked. Which configuration fits, and what must they ensure?

options.A: No Model Armor for two weeks, then enable blocking directly
options.B: Inspect-only enforcement, ensuring Cloud Logging captures the findings
options.C: Inspect and block, with an allow list of known-good prompts
options.D: Inspect-only with logging disabled to reduce cost during the trial

rationale.A: Provides no data about false positives before enforcement.
rationale.B: Inspect-only logs violations without blocking, and its value depends on Cloud Logging being in place to review findings.
rationale.C: Blocks traffic during the evaluation window, which the team wanted to avoid.
rationale.D: Without logs there is no evidence to review.

stem: A new team is deciding which Agent Gateway mode to enable for two paths: developers' IDE clients calling internal agents, and those agents calling a third-party API. The architect must first state precisely which traffic each mode governs. Which description is correct?

options.A: Ingress governs clients calling agents; egress governs agents calling anything
options.B: Ingress governs agent-to-agent calls; egress governs user traffic from browsers
options.C: Ingress applies to Gemini Enterprise only; egress applies to Agent Runtime only
options.D: Ingress governs calls into Google Cloud APIs; egress governs calls to Gemini models

rationale.A: Client-to-Agent (ingress) secures clients calling agents and tools on Google Cloud; Agent-to-Anywhere (egress) secures agents calling servers, agents, tools or APIs anywhere.
rationale.B: Reverses the definitions.
rationale.C: Gemini Enterprise supports egress; Agent Runtime supports both modes.
rationale.D: Neither mode is defined by the API being called.

stem: A company wants agent traffic subject to its existing data-exfiltration perimeter, with ingress and egress rules that name agents specifically. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Perimeters apply only to human users, not to workloads
options.B: Agents must run outside perimeters because certificates rotate daily
options.C: VPC Service Controls cannot reference agents, only service accounts
options.D: Agent Identity integrates with VPC Service Controls for perimeter protection

rationale.A: VPC-SC governs API access by principals including workloads.
rationale.B: Rotation does not conflict with perimeter membership.
rationale.C: Agent identities can be named in perimeter rules.
rationale.D: Agent Identity is integrated with policy systems including IAM, PAB and VPC Service Controls, with agent principals usable in perimeter rules.

stem: A healthcare analytics company already runs a large GKE platform with GPU node pools and a mature SRE team. It wants to serve a Gemma model for an internal agent at steady, high throughput, reuse its existing cluster tooling, and tune the serving stack itself. Which option fits?

options.A: Run the model inside the agent's Cloud Run container on CPU only to avoid GPUs
options.B: Use a serverless model-as-a-service endpoint so the SRE team no longer operates the model
options.C: Deploy the model to Agent Runtime as an agent so it scales with the agent
options.D: Serve Gemma on GKE with vLLM on GPU node pools

rationale.A: CPU-only inference for steady high throughput is slow and costly.
rationale.B: Removes the control the team explicitly wants to keep and reuse.
rationale.C: Agent Runtime hosts agents, not a tunable model-serving stack.
rationale.D: Google documents serving Gemma on GKE with vLLM on supported GPUs, which fits a team that wants to reuse and tune its own cluster.

stem: A user explicitly clicks 'Remember that I am allergic to peanuts' in a food-ordering app. The team wants this stored as a memory immediately and exactly, without waiting for extraction from the conversation. Which Memory Bank operation fits?

options.A: An app:allergy key so every session sees it
options.B: GenerateMemories on the next session, then check the result
options.C: A temp:allergy key set in the current invocation
options.D: CreateMemory, writing the fact directly to Memory Bank

rationale.A: app: state is shared across all users, leaking one user's allergy.
rationale.B: Extraction may paraphrase or delay a safety-critical fact.
rationale.C: temp: state is discarded after the invocation.
rationale.D: CreateMemory lets agents write memories directly, alongside GenerateMemories from conversation history.

stem: In a three-agent chain, the user asks agent A, which delegates to B, which calls a tool through C. Auditors must be able to see which agent acted and on whose behalf at each hop. What supports this?

options.A: Per-agent identities whose logs record the agent and the user identity
options.B: Cloud Trace spans alone, which carry the caller's email at every hop
options.C: One shared service account with the agent name in the user-agent header
options.D: A correlation ID added by each agent to its own application logs

rationale.A: With Agent Identity, when agents act on a user's behalf logs show both the agent's and the user's identities.
rationale.B: Traces show timing and structure, not authenticated identity of each agent.
rationale.C: Headers are not authenticated identity and can be spoofed.
rationale.D: Application conventions are weaker than platform-recorded identity and are easy to omit.

stem: An architect proposes Cloud Scheduler and Pub/Sub to coordinate the steps of a user-facing agent conversation that must answer within seconds. What is the main problem?

options.A: They require a GKE cluster, which the team does not have
options.B: Pub/Sub cannot carry JSON payloads produced by agents
options.C: They are asynchronous, not request-time orchestration
options.D: Cloud Scheduler is limited to one job per project per minute

rationale.A: Both are serverless; the mismatch is architectural.
rationale.B: Pub/Sub carries arbitrary payloads; latency and ordering are the real issue.
rationale.C: Scheduling and messaging services introduce queuing and delivery latency; in-request orchestration belongs in the agent framework.
rationale.D: Not the relevant constraint.

stem: In a repository that contains production Terraform, a lead wants the Antigravity CLI agent to run `git` and `npm test` freely but to never run `rm -rf`, and to ask before any other command. How should this be configured?

options.A: A hook that deletes the Terraform directory from the agent's view at startup
options.B: strict mode for everything, with the developer approving git and npm test each time
options.C: always-proceed mode, with a rule in AGENTS.md telling the agent to avoid rm -rf
options.D: request-review mode, with an allow list for git and npm test and a deny list for rm -rf

rationale.A: Hides files instead of controlling commands, and still allows rm -rf elsewhere.
rationale.B: Safe but ignores the requirement that git and npm test run freely.
rationale.C: Rules are advisory; always-proceed would run anything else without asking.
rationale.D: Antigravity supports request-review, always-proceed and strict modes plus allow/deny lists such as command(git) and command(rm -rf).

stem: A newly launched agent shows three symptoms: occasional 10-second responses, one tool failing 5% of the time, and rising cost. The team has one week. Which approach gives the most reliable improvement?

options.A: Escalate to the model provider before investigating internally
options.B: Start with the cheapest fix regardless of impact
options.C: Fix all three at once with a single large refactor
options.D: Quantify each symptom from traces and fix in order of user impact

rationale.A: The symptoms point at the team's own tools and design.
rationale.B: Optimises for effort rather than user outcomes.
rationale.C: Couples changes and makes it impossible to attribute improvements.
rationale.D: Measuring first and ranking by impact directs limited time at the problems that matter, using the trace data already available.

stem: A team implementing human-in-the-loop in ADK wants the agent to pause at a specific tool, show the reviewer what will happen, and continue only after approval, with no external workflow engine. What should they use?

options.A: A Cloud Workflows step that calls the agent back after approval
options.B: An instruction telling the agent to wait for the word 'approved'
options.C: ADK tool confirmation, which pauses the tool until the user responds
options.D: A Pub/Sub topic the reviewer publishes to, polled by the agent

rationale.A: Adds the external engine the team wanted to avoid.
rationale.B: The model can proceed anyway; nothing technically pauses the tool.
rationale.C: ADK's tool confirmation feature lets a tool pause execution and interact with a user for confirmation before proceeding.
rationale.D: Custom plumbing for a built-in capability.

stem: Different teams have registered MCP servers whose tools overlap, and an orchestrator must choose reliable ones. Which Agent Registry capability helps the orchestrator use standardised integration?

options.A: Ranking tools by popularity so the orchestrator always picks the most used
options.B: Locating endpoints through standardised MCP or A2A
options.C: Executing tools on behalf of agents so orchestrators need no clients
options.D: Automatically merging duplicate tools into one canonical entry

rationale.A: Not a described capability.
rationale.B: Agent Registry lets you use standardized MCP or A2A protocols to locate and connect to functional endpoints, reducing infrastructure overhead.
rationale.C: Registry is a catalog; execution happens at the endpoints.
rationale.D: The registry catalogs entries; it does not merge tools for you.

stem: A research agent delegates a five-minute literature review to a remote A2A agent. The user interface should show partial results as they appear rather than waiting. Which A2A interaction pattern fits?

options.A: Push notifications to a webhook, which the browser receives directly
options.B: Request/response polling every 30 seconds until completion
options.C: Streaming with server-sent events for incremental results
options.D: Opening one WebSocket per artifact produced by the remote agent

rationale.A: Push notifications target server-side webhooks, not the user's browser session.
rationale.B: Polling is supported but shows nothing between polls and adds latency.
rationale.C: A2A supports streaming with SSE so clients receive real-time, incremental results.
rationale.D: Not the documented A2A transport pattern.

stem: An agent passes its evalset in CI, yet quality complaints rise two months after launch as user phrasing and the product catalogue change. Which practice addresses this specific gap?

options.A: Continuous evaluation on sampled production traffic against the golden set
options.B: Adding more unit tests for the agent's tool functions
options.C: Raising the CI pass threshold from 80% to 95%
options.D: Running the same CI evalset more frequently, for example hourly

rationale.A: Continuous evaluation pipelines detect drift after release, which a fixed pre-merge suite cannot see.
rationale.B: Unit tests verify code, not agent behaviour against changing inputs.
rationale.C: A stricter gate on stale cases does not detect drift.
rationale.D: The same fixed cases cannot reveal changes in real traffic.

stem: A payments agent must never call `issue_refund` without first calling `verify_identity`. Which evaluation approach best enforces this as a release criterion?

options.A: Manual review of a sample of refunds each month
options.B: Trajectory evaluation cases asserting verify_identity precedes issue_refund
options.C: A rubric asking a judge whether the answer sounds compliant
options.D: An alert on refunds issued without a preceding verification log entry

rationale.A: Sampling after the fact is not a release gate.
rationale.B: Continuous evaluation of tool execution against success criteria catches ordering violations before release.
rationale.C: Judging tone does not verify the call sequence.
rationale.D: Production detection, not pre-release prevention.

stem: A team screens both user prompts and model responses with Model Armor and wants to follow documented best practice for configuration. What should they do?

options.A: Use one template for both, so settings never diverge
options.B: Screen only responses to save tokens on the prompt side
options.C: Screen only prompts, since responses come from a trusted model
options.D: Use separate templates for prompts and for responses

rationale.A: Prompts and responses carry different risks and warrant different settings.
rationale.B: Prompt injection arrives in prompts, which would then go unscreened.
rationale.C: Responses can contain sensitive or harmful content and are screened too.
rationale.D: The documentation recommends separate Model Armor templates for user prompts and model responses.

stem: A platform team plans to register every internal API as a governed destination behind one Agent Gateway instance. They estimate 7,000 resources. What should they know?

options.A: There is no limit, but latency grows linearly with the number of resources
options.B: Only MCP servers count toward the limit, so APIs can be added freely
options.C: A gateway instance supports at most 5,000 registered resources
options.D: Registered resources are limited to 500 per project across all gateways

rationale.A: A documented maximum exists.
rationale.B: The limit applies to registered resources generally.
rationale.C: Agent Gateway documents a maximum of 5,000 registered resources per gateway instance.
rationale.D: Not the documented limit.

stem: An agent computes shipping dates and is occasionally off by one day for orders placed late at night. Traces show the model called the date tool correctly with the values it was given. Where is the defect most likely?

options.A: In the retrieval corpus, which lacks a shipping-policy document
options.B: In the tool's own timezone handling, not in the model's reasoning
options.C: In the model's arithmetic, which should be replaced with a larger model
options.D: In the session state, which loses the order timestamp overnight

rationale.A: This is a computation defect, not a knowledge gap.
rationale.B: When tool inputs are correct and outputs are wrong, the defect is in the tool implementation, which ordinary unit tests can catch.
rationale.C: The model delegated the computation to the tool.
rationale.D: The tool received the values, so state carried them.
